entities.name: Fabrizio I Colonna
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Fabrizio I Colonna (died 1520-04-04) was a preeminent Italian condottiero and a scion of the powerful Colonna family, whose military prowess and strategic acumen profoundly influenced the course of the Italian Wars during the late 15th and early 16th centuries. Operating primarily in the service of the Spanish crown, he was a pivotal figure in the shift from medieval mercenary armies to the more disciplined, gunpowder-era forces that defined early modern European warfare. His career intersected with the ambitions of Ferdinand II of Aragon, Louis XII of France, and Emperor Charles V, placing him at the heart of the geopolitical struggle for control over the Italian peninsula.

Colonna's military career was marked by a series of high-stakes campaigns and battles that reshaped the map of Italy. He distinguished himself at the Battle of Garigliano in 1503, where, alongside Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba, the "Great Captain," his leadership contributed significantly to the decisive Spanish victory over the French, establishing Spanish hegemony in the Kingdom of Naples. Despite being captured by Gaston of Foix at the Battle of Ravenna in 1512, a major French triumph, Colonna quickly returned to service, leading papal and Spanish forces to victory against the Venetians at La Motta (Vicenza) in 1513, further solidifying his reputation as a formidable commander.

His contributions extended beyond individual victories; Colonna was instrumental in the practical application of evolving military doctrines, particularly the integration of pike and shot formations that characterized the Spanish *tercio*. His leadership helped to transition Italian warfare from reliance on heavy cavalry to a more infantry-centric model, directly influencing the development of early modern armies. The Colonna family's power, already substantial, was further enhanced by Fabrizio's military achievements, ensuring their continued influence in Roman and Neapolitan politics for generations.
